Revision 002 changes only test_dart_codec.c (#ifdef NDEBUG #error guard), test_codec.py (the '-DNDEBUG -E' negative check) and README.
reviewed.references: PROVENANCE pins re-hashed and matching: m1n1 dart.c c650a8aa, dart.h e1dcfb1b, dart8020.py 497b7a64; linux-aurora apple-dart.c ebbd0250, io-pgtable-dart.c d2079a0e, pcie-apple.c 3ed38395.

verdict: APPROVE the frozen codec as an original, bounded, host-only software model. Every encoded format fact matches the pinned primary sources, restricted to a stricter canonical T8103 subset. The widths, limits and range arithmetic are correct and overflow-free, outputs are preserved on every non-success path, and the graph validation is complete and bounded. The ARM64 object has no undefined imports, no data section and small frames. No defects found; notes N1-N7 are non-blocking.
format_facts: Entry and granule: 8-byte little-endian entries, 2048 per 16K table (m1n1 dart.c SZ_16K tables; dart8020.py PAGE_BITS 14, IDX_BITS 11). dld_word_load/store are explicit LE byte loops with an exact size of 8.

IOVA split: m1n1 C dart_map_page uses l1_index = (iova>>25)&0x1fff, ttbr = idx>>11, l2 = (iova>>14)&0x7ff (dart.c:762-765, :726-729); Python uses L0_OFF 36 / L1_OFF 25 / L2_OFF 14. With Linux's T8020/T8103 ias = 32 (apple-dart.c:3094) this means TTBR0 only, L1 index 0..127 (bits 31:25), L2 bits 24:14, offset bits 13:0. The codec matches: split_iova rejects iova >= 2^32 rather than truncating, root is always 0, validate refuses nonzero root entries at index >= 128, and TTBR1..3 must be zero.

TTBR: m1n1 DART_T8020_TTBR_VALID BIT(31), ADDR GENMASK(30,0), SHIFT 12 (dart.c:50-52). The codec emits bit31 | PA>>12. With PA < 2^36 and 16K-aligned, PA>>12 occupies only bits 23:2, so TTBR_ALLOWED 0x80fffffc is exact for this profile. Decode rejects bits 30:24 (PA >= 2^36) and bits 1:0 (sub-16K).

Table pointer: m1n1 C writes FIELD_PREP(offset_mask, pa>>14) | DART_PTE_VALID (dart.c:711-712, :749), and Linux dart_install_table writes paddr_to_iopte(table) | APPLE_DART_PTE_VALID (io-pgtable-dart.c:147). The codec's canonical PA|bit0 matches. m1n1 Python's occasional bit1 on L1 entries is correctly rejected as non-canonical (documented).

Leaf: m1n1 dart_t8020.pte_flags = SP_END 0xfff | SP_START 0 | DISABLE_SP bit1 | VALID (dart.c:177-180, SP_START 63:52 and SP_END 51:40 at :55-56), and Linux sets SUBPAGE_START 0, SUBPAGE_END 0xfff, VALID and APPLE_DART1_PTE_PROT_SP_DIS (io-pgtable-dart.c:129-132, :205-212). The codec's LEAF_FIXED is bit0|bit1|0x000fff0000000000. Any SP_START bit or other unlisted bit is rejected.

Physical width: m1n1's generic T8020 offset is 39:14, Linux APPLE_DART1_PADDR_MASK is 35:12 and apple_dart_hw_t8103.oas = 36 (apple-dart.c:3368-3373). The codec's PA_MASK 35:14 with 16K alignment is the T8103 intersection, and higher bits are rejected rather than masked. DLD_PA_LIMIT 2^36 covers the T8103 DRAM window.

Permissions: Linux APPLE_DART1_PTE_PROT_NO_READ BIT(8) and NO_WRITE BIT(7) (io-pgtable-dart.c:54-55), applied inversely in dart_prot_to_pte (:205-212). The codec encodes and decodes exactly these, accepts R, W and RW, and rejects the no-access encoding and empty or unknown access requests.

Streams and RID: dart8020.py TCR irange(0x100,16,4) and TTBR (16 streams x 4) plus Linux max_sid_count 16 give SID < 16. pcie-apple.c t8103_hw.max_rid2sid = 64 (:255-263) with no sid_indexed_rid2sid, and slots are found by free-slot allocation (:2061-2066) after a RAZ/WI probe (:1734-1743), so slot < 64 with an arbitrary index is consistent. PORT_RID2SID packs VALID bit31 | SID<<16 | BDF (:198-203, :2067). dld_rid forms bus<<8|dev<<3|fn = pci_dev_id after full BDF bounds.

MSI: Linux reserves the doorbell page (DOORBELL_ADDR & PAGE_MASK, IOMMU_RESV_MSI, apple-dart.c:2631-2645). The codec denies the whole 16K page [0xffffc000, 2^32) holding the ADT-reported doorbell 0xfffff000, a superset of a 4K-page reservation and equal to a 16K-page kernel's. The APCIE0 window [0x100000, 0xbff00000) comes from the existing ADT report and is caller-supplied, never defaulted (DLD_APCIE_* are informational).

code_review.range_arithmetic: dld_range_check rejects limit 0, size 0, base >= limit and size > limit - base, so it has no overflow. overlaps/contains run only on ranges already checked as nonempty and nonwrapping below 2^36 (PA) or 2^32 (IOVA); contains compares 'b.base - a.base <= a.size - b.size' after b.base >= a.base and b.size <= a.size. Validation iovas reach at most (127<<25)|(2047<<14) = 0xffffc000, so iova + 16K <= 2^32. The translate page base is iova & ~0x3fff with a 64-bit mask.
code_review.graph: dld_validate requires: <= 129 tables, each with non-null bytes, size exactly 16K and level ROOT or LEAF_TABLE; at most one ROOT, at the TTBR0 PA; table pages aligned, inside one RAM interval and clear of every reservation; no duplicate table PA; each L1 child an existing LEAF_TABLE referenced once (shared or cyclic refused, and the root cannot be a child because of its level); every table reachable (no orphans); leaves canonical, IOVA page inside the aperture and outside the MSI page, leaf page allowed, not equal to any table page (equality is full overlap for aligned 16K pages), <= 256 leaves, and no duplicate leaf PA. An all-zero TTBR set with zero tables validates as empty. Validation is total over every entry, not lazy.
code_review.bounds: A worst-case validate reads 2048 + 128x2048 = 264,192 entries. The per-leaf work (find_table <= 129, pairwise <= 255, policy <= 128) is capped at 257 leaves by the LIMIT check placed before the pairwise scan. The references[129] and leaf_pa[256] indices stay in range.
code_review.output_preservation: Every encode/decode, split_iova and word store writes its output only on DLD_OK. dld_validate writes *stats only at success (a local result). dld_translate writes *pa only after validate, decode and permission checks succeed. UNMAPPED (TTBR0 zero, L1 zero or leaf zero) returns before writing. Only scratch changes on failure, as documented.
code_review.translate: Revalidates the full snapshot, then indexes tables already proven present. An IOVA outside the aperture is DLD_RANGE, the MSI page is DLD_OVERLAP, an empty image or missing entry is DLD_UNMAPPED, and a missing access right is DLD_PERMISSION; pa = leaf.pa + offset stays below 2^36.
code_review.bindings: count <= 64; first_bus <= last_bus <= 255; RID <= 0xffff with its bus inside the bounds; SID < 16; slot < 64; RID, SID and slot pairwise distinct (exclusive-stream model; Linux's shared Wi-Fi/BT stream is deliberately refused).
code_review.pointer_lifetime: The C contract is explicit and checkable only as preconditions: non-null where required (checked), each table's bytes readable for its declared 16K, all inputs immutable during the call, scratch, outputs and inputs non-aliasing, normal memory only (never device memory), and serialized access. No global or static state exists (the object has only __text), so concurrent calls on disjoint scratch are reentrant.

object: nm -m: 13 external dld_* plus the static allowed_page, with no undefined symbols, so no compiler-emitted memcpy/memset in a freestanding build. One __text section (0xfc0 bytes), no data or bss. Stack adjustments: dld_validate 0xa0 (160 bytes), dld_translate 0x50 (80 bytes), others leaf/frameless. The translate-to-validate chain is about 240 bytes, well under the 1024 frame warning. dld_scratch (2184 bytes) is caller-provided.
tests_rerun: In a scratch copy of the directory: test_codec.py --mutations gives HOST_SOFTWARE_CODEC_CHECKS_PASS: 11 groups, 4096 seeded roundtrips, 9 compiling mutants rejected (leaf/TTBR reserved bits, IOVA truncation, read permission, MSI page, physical alias, high root entry, orphan table, stream width), and NDEBUG refused at the explicit guard. Same source hashes. The production directory was not used for build artifacts.

notes.text: PROVENANCE line citations are close but sometimes off by one region: dart.c:49 is TTBR_OFF (VALID/ADDR/SHIFT are :50-52); io-pgtable-dart.c:364 is a declaration (the TTBR-count comment is just above); apple-dart.c:3092 is the switch (ias=32 and num_streams are :3094-3097); dart8020.py:77 and :90 cite TCR and L0_OFF in a file whose relevant definitions span :44-96. The facts are correct.
DLD_MAX_BINDINGS is 64 (the slot space), but distinct SIDs below 16 cap a passing set at 16 bindings. This is expected for the exclusive-stream model; the README could say so.
dld_scratch is about 2.2 KiB. A future XNU adapter should hold it in a per-DART, lock-protected structure rather than on a 16 KiB kernel stack in deep I/O paths.

dld_translate revalidates the whole snapshot (up to about 264k entry loads) on every call. That is bounded and correct for a model, but a kernel adapter needs a validated immutable snapshot or incremental validation under its publication protocol, not per-DMA revalidation.

IOVA page 0 is mappable if a caller's aperture includes it. The APCIE0 aperture starts at 0x100000, so this is unaffected; an adapter policy should keep IOVA 0 unused if XNU or IOMapper treats it as a null DMA sentinel.

The canonical-only decoder rejects firmware or m1n1-Python forms (bit1 on L1 entries, subpage ranges, 4K or wider forms). Preserving firmware-owned tables (README step 1) needs a separate read-only inspector. Do not widen this validator.

The slot count must come from the per-port RAZ/WI probe (Linux discovers it, up to 64). SIDs are per DART/port namespace. dld_bindings_check validates one port's table and is caller policy, not discovery or ownership.

scope: Read-only source, provenance, object and host-test review. Tests ran on a scratch copy only. Astra's m1-dart-survey prototype, active kernels and hosts were not touched.
